polls.quote: Voters approve 53 – 13 percent of the job Mayor de Blasio has done so far, with 34 percent undecided, the independent Quinnipiac (KWIN-uh-pe-ack) University poll finds. [...] From January 9 – 15, Quinnipiac University surveyed 1,288 New York City voters, with a margin of error of +/- 2.7 percentage points.
polls.notes: Q1 table: Approve 53%, Disapprove 13, DK/NA 34. Quinnipiac 'New York City voters' = registered voters.

polls.sponsor: The Wall Street Journal/NBC 4 New York
polls.quote: 39% of registered voters in New York City approve of the job Mayor de Blasio is doing in office. This includes 10% who think he is doing an excellent job and 29% who say he is doing a good one. 37% rate de Blasio’s performance as fair while one in five voters -- 20% -- thinks he is performing poorly. Five percent have either never heard of de Blasio or are unsure how to rate him. [...] This survey of 785 New York City adults was conducted February 27th through March 4th, 2014 [...] There are 586 registered voters.
polls.notes: Grade question ('Would you rate the job Mayor Bill de Blasio is doing in office as excellent, good, fair, or poor?'), asked of registered voters only; no adults-only version of the job rating in the tables. 785 adults interviewed in total.

polls.quote: New York City voters approve 45 – 34 percent of the job Mayor Bill de Blasio is doing, below Police Commissioner William Bratton’s 57 – 13 percent approval rating and City Comptroller Scott Stringer’s 53 – 12 percent score, according to a Quinnipiac University poll released today. [...] From March 12 – 17, Quinnipiac University surveyed 1,234 New York City voters, with a margin of error of +/- 2.8 percentage points.

Siena College New York City Poll Trends – December 2014 / Q. 1 Do you approve or disapprove of the way Bill de Blasio is handling his job as Mayor ? / DATE APPROVE DISAPPROVE DON’T KNOW/NO OPINION / December 2014 52 32 15 / April 2014 49 31 19. [Release text:] By a 52-32 percent margin, New Yorkers approve of the way de Blasio is handling his job as mayor, virtually unchanged from 49-31 percent in April.
polls.notes: PARTIAL VERIFICATION. Numbers come from the trend table in Siena's own December 12, 2014 release PDF, not from the April 2014 release itself, which is not on sri.siena.edu (checked the 2014 archive pages 1-5, the April 2014 monthly archive, the site search for 'de Blasio', and guessed PDF/crosstab URLs: all absent or 404). Population 'adults' inferred because the trend table compares residents to residents; the release date, field dates (March 29–April 3) and sample (news reports give 1,190 adults / 941 registered voters) come from news coverage and are NOT verified on a pollster page. Treat the date fields as approximate.

polls.quote: New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio’s job approval rating is up to 51 – 28 percent, but the gap between approval by black and white voters persists, according to a Quinnipiac University poll released today. [...] From June 5 – 9, Quinnipiac University surveyed 1,033 New York City voters, with a margin of error of +/- 3.1 percentage points.
polls.notes: Q1 table: Approve 51%, Disapprove 28, DK/NA 21. The companion June 12, 2014 release (nyc06122014_yde82k.pdf, same fieldwork) covers police questions and does not repeat the mayoral approval question. The 'known lead' of 50% approve for June was wrong: 51–28.

polls.quote: New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio clings to a 50 – 32 percent job approval rating, marked by a continuing divide between black and white voters, according to a Quinnipiac University poll released today. [...] From August 20 – 25, Quinnipiac University surveyed 1,021 New York City voters, with a margin of error of +/- 3.1 percentage points.

New York City voters approve 71 – 26 percent of Mayor Bill de Blasio’s decision to decriminalize possession of small amounts of marijuana, but give the mayor an overall 49 – 36 percent job approval rating, according to a Quinnipiac University poll released today. [...] From November 12 – 17, Quinnipiac University surveyed 1,164 New York City voters, with a margin of error of +/- 2.9 percentage points.

By a 52-32 percent margin, New Yorkers approve of the way de Blasio is handling his job as mayor, virtually unchanged from 49-31 percent in April. [...] This New York Times/Siena College Poll was conducted December 4-10, 2014 by telephone calls in both English and Spanish to 760 New York City residents of whom 621 are registered voters. It has a margin of error of +3.6 percentage points for residents and +3.9 for registered voters.
polls.notes: Headline figure is among all residents (adults). Crosstabs give the registered-voter column separately (next entry).

polls.quote: Q1. Do you approve or disapprove of the way Bill de Blasio is handling his job as Mayor? [...] 621 New York City Registered Voters, MOE +/- 3.9% [...] Reg Voter column: Approve 53%, Disapprove 34%, Don't know/No opinion 13%.
polls.notes: Registered-voter subsample from the crosstabs PDF; the Total (residents) column reads 52/32/15.

polls.quote: New York City voters disapprove 56 – 36 percent of the way Mayor Bill de Blasio is handling relations between the police and the community and give him a 47 – 38 percent overall job approval rating, according to a Quinnipiac University poll released today. [...] From December 10 – 16, Quinnipiac University surveyed 1,374 New York City voters, with a margin of error of +/- 2.6 percentage points.
polls.notes: Q1 table: Approve 47%, Disapprove 38, DK/NA 15. Trend table in this release confirms the whole 2014 Quinnipiac series: Dec 18 47/38, Nov 18 49/36, Aug 26 50/32, Jun 11 51/28, Mar 18 45/34, Jan 16 53/13. The companion Dec 17, 2014 release (nyc12172014_Ngs43nk.pdf) covers Garner protests and does not include the job-approval question.

unverified.reported: 49% approve / 31% disapprove; news reports cite March 29–April 3 fieldwork, 1,190 adults incl. 941 registered voters
unverified.status: Standalone release not on sri.siena.edu. Numbers ARE confirmed via the trend table in Siena's December 12, 2014 release PDF and are recorded in 'polls' with a PARTIAL VERIFICATION flag; field dates and sample size remain unverified on a pollster page.
attempts: two WebSearch passes restricted to siena.edu

unverified.reported: The task brief suggested Marist/NY1 January 2014 and later releases.
unverified.status: No evidence any exist. Marist's May 2015 NYC release says the 44% rating is 'up slightly from 39% in March 2014' and its trend table lists only March 2014 as a prior reading, so Marist appears to have polled NYC on de Blasio's job rating only once in 2014 (March 7). Marist's '12/23' NYC release is December 2013, before inauguration. News coverage of a Marist '35% vs 38% in November' reading is April 2016 / November 2015, not 2014.
No NYT/CBS citywide poll of de Blasio in 2014 surfaced; the Times' 2014 NYC partner was Siena (with NY1 in April). nytimes.com not attempted.

self_audit: Every Quinnipiac entry was read from the PDF on poll.qu.edu (text extracted locally with pypdf; the release text, the Q1 table with DK/NA and the methodology line were all checked, and the December 18 trend table matches each entry). Marist March 2014 was read from both the HTML release and the tables PDF on maristpoll.marist.edu; the job-rating table exists only for registered voters. Siena December 2014 was read from the HTML post, the release PDF and the crosstabs PDF on sri.siena.edu; adults and RV are recorded separately. Siena April 2014 is the weak point: the numbers are on a pollster page (the December trend table) but the release itself is missing from Siena's site, so dates and n are from news coverage and are flagged. No web.archive.org copies were used (the fetch tool cannot reach it). Quinnipiac HTML release pages at poll.qu.edu/poll-release?releaseid=N render for 2050 (June 11) and 2120 (December 18) and are listed as html_url; the other IDs were not located, so the PDF is the URL of record. Known-lead correction: June 2014 Quinnipiac is 51–28, not 50; the 50–32 reading is August 26.
